payload.description_html:
The crocodile lantern ( Lampanyctus crocodilus ) is a fish found in the Mediterranean, recognizable by its oblique mouth and long, thin caudal peduncle.

The MEDITS surveys provide spatial information on demersal species in terms of population and community indices, demographic structures and life history traits. Since 1994, these fisheries surveys have been conducted jointly by Spanish, Italian and French partners. These annual surveys (May-June) study five depth strata, defined for all sectors: 10-50 m, 50-100 m, 100-200 m, 200-500 m and 500-800 m. All the species collected including the benthos are sorted, weighed and counted. For 84 species, measurements are also taken and on 41 of these species (32 selachians, 3 bony fish, 4 crustaceans, 2 cephalopods) all the individual parameters are collected.
